problem: Which of the following is the graph of $y={6}^{x-2}+3?$
worked_solution:
To plot the given function, we follow these steps:

- First, we plot the graph of $y={6}^{x}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/565fbb4450ba8feb0b1184cb18442ca00f9ce24d42d3d3243cfcc9aa82b62d23.png)

- To plot $y={6}^{x-2},$ we shift the graph of $y={6}^{x}$ horizontally by $2$ units to the right. The $y$-intercept moves from $(0,1)$ to $(2,1),$ but the horizontal asymptote stays at $y=0.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/0656969561de20752caa691f247f95f1daa743bb8bf167470e98c5d739b82b64.png)

- To plot $y={6}^{x-2}+3,$ we shift the graph of $y={6}^{x-2}$ vertically by $3$ units up. The point $(2,1)$ moves to $(2,4)$ and the horizontal asymptote moves from $y=0$ to $y=3.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13943741/assets/cf548121c884efcd7a36bc3282ae64d696f9de2da64b954bc2fa962376819477.png)
